title: Extended Single-Atom Tweezer Arrays in High-Cooperativity Cavity-QED
authors: Thomas Picot, Clément Raphin, Marcel Kern, Pierre-Antoine Bourdel, Théo Ahamdach, Jakob Reichel, Romain Long
abstract: A central challenge for cavity-QED-based quantum technologies is to make high-cooperativity optical interfaces compatible with site-resolved arrays of single atoms. Here, we demonstrate optical tweezer arrays of individual $^{87}$Rb atoms inside a fiber Fabry-Perot microcavity with single-atom cooperativity $\mathcal{C} \sim 90$. We combine background-free site-resolved fluorescence imaging of extended arrays with collective coupling to a common cavity mode for arrays with a mean atom number up to $\bar{N} \simeq 36$. These results establish a high-cooperativity platform for many-body cavity-QED with site-resolved detection and control.
summary: The research demonstrates a robust platform for many-body cavity quantum electrodynamics using arrays of single $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ atoms trapped in optical tweezers near a microcavity. By combining site-resolved fluorescence imaging with measurements of collective vacuum Rabi splitting, the authors establish that high cooperativity can be maintained across extended atomic ensembles. This paves the way for scalable quantum simulation and computation utilizing cavity coupling.
main_problem: To establish a high-cooperativity platform for many-body cavity-QED that is compatible with site-resolved detection across extended arrays of single atoms.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated high single-atom cooperativity ($C \simeq 88$) and maintained compatibility for collective coupling in large arrays (up to $ ar{N} \simeq 36$), enabling many-body cavity control with local readout.
method: The experiment combines optical tweezer trapping of $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ atoms, site-resolved fluorescence imaging using a background-free two-photon scheme, and measurement of collective vacuum Rabi splitting in a fiber Fabry-Perot microcavity.
model_or_system: The physical system is an array of individual $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ atoms trapped by optical tweezers and coupled to the quantized electromagnetic field mode of a high-finesse fiber Fabry-Perot cavity. The coupling regime is characterized by the cooperativity parameter $C$.
key_observables: Single-atom cooperativity ($C$), detection fidelity for hyperfine states, mean atom number ($ ar{N}$), and collective vacuum Rabi splitting spectrum.
important_parameters: Single-atom cooperativity $\mathcal{C} \sim 90$; Mean atom number up to $\simeq 36$; Detection fidelities $>98.8\%$.
main_assumptions: The primary limitations noted are the state detection fidelity being limited by hyperfine-state lifetime and preparation imperfection, rather than intrinsic readout discrimination.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup, cavity mode mapping, vacuum Rabi splitting measurements confirming coupling strength for various array sizes (e.g., 20-site chain), and detailed characterization of background-free fluorescence imaging fidelity across the array.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first demonstrating high single-atom cooperativity, then validating site-resolved detection compatibility over extended arrays, and finally characterizing the collective coupling strength as a function of array geometry (1D chains to 2D lattices).
why_interesting: This work pushes the boundaries of cavity QED by merging two challenging aspects: scaling up atom numbers while maintaining strong light-matter interaction ($C$), and achieving high-fidelity, local readout simultaneously.
